corrected_value.title: The Benefit of Becoming Friends: Complaining after Service Failures Leads Customers with Strong Ties to Increase Loyalty

decisions.quote:
Final Report  –  Umashankar_JournMarket_2017_Ej3y_65km6
Replication team: Ernest Baskin
Replication OSF: https://osf.io/skj4c/
Claim for Review – The claim selected was that strongly tied customers who complain (vs. withhold feedback) after a service failure will increase their loyalty. In contrast, for weakly tied customers, complaining has no effect on loyalty.
decisions.reason: The SCORE Final Report header ('Umashankar_JournMarket_2017_Ej3y_65km6') names first author Umashankar, Journal of Marketing, and year 2017, and the Claim for Review states the exact focal claim from the title of the shipped original (Umashankar, Ward, & Dahl, 2017, 'The Benefit of Becoming Friends: Complaining after Service Failures Leads Customers with Strong Ties to Increase Loyalty', DOI 10.1509/jm.16.0125). Blind coding captured the same single target (target_index 0) with year 2017 but omitted the author name from the report header, which prevented automated target pairing.

decisions.quote: Stage 2: H* was not supported as the interaction term on the overall ANOVA was not significant. In addition, the pattern of means in the strong ties group was not consistent but the pattern of means in the weak ties group was consistent. The results for the interaction are as follows: [F(1,948)= .219, p=.640, f-squared = .000]. In addition, no deviations from the preregistration occurred.
decisions.reason: With the tested original identity resolved to Umashankar et al. (2017) (blind target_index 0), both Stage 1 (F(1,435) = .003, p = .954) and Stage 2 (F(1,948) = .219, p = .640) explicitly conclude that the focal interaction hypothesis H* was not supported. Under Codebook Rule 1, the authors' explicit verdict that H* was not supported governs; a consistent null pattern of means within the weak-ties subgroup is merely one condition of the failed two-way interaction test and does not make the outcome mixed.

decisions.quote: As of 8/20/2021, stage 1 data collection has been completed, and the stage 1 analytic sample size was exceeded (439 participants after exclusions). As of 8/26/2021, stage 2 data collection has been completed, and the stage 2 analytic sample size was met (952 participants after exclusions).
decisions.reason: The study collected new data across two completed stages (N = 439 in Stage 1 and N = 952 in Stage 2 after exclusions) to re-test the published focal interaction finding of Umashankar et al. (2017), which is a replication under both shipped and blind coding.
